title: Infusion Center: Chair 4 Chemo Hydration, Pocket Restricted

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Infusion Center Front Desk

callee.name: Chief Nursing Officer (CMO and Clinical Pharmacy Manager conferenced in)
callee.label: Command Center, Conference Room C

transcript.speaker: Infusion Center Manager
transcript.text: Hi, it's Carla Moreno in the infusion center. Is the CMO on? Good. And pharmacy? Okay. I'll be quick, I've got a full room.

transcript.speaker: Infusion Center Manager
transcript.text: We've moved 9 of today's 22 appointments. They're all routine hydration. We started them on oral fluids first, and the physicians' offices have rebooked them for next week. That part's done.

transcript.speaker: Infusion Center Manager
transcript.text: Here's my problem. I have a 58-year-old woman in Chair 4 who's due for chemotherapy today. Her protocol needs IV hydration before and after, and today is her protocol day. Oncology says it can't be delayed. Not to next week, not to Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Infusion Center Manager
transcript.text: And my cabinet's 1000 mL NS pocket says RESTRICTED. My nurses can't pull it. She's already in the chair with her IV in, and her husband is asking me why we're waiting.

transcript.speaker: Infusion Center Manager
transcript.text: So I need to know right now. Who decides whether she gets her bags? Is that pharmacy, is that the CMO, is that me? I don't want my nurses calling three people every time this comes up today.

transcript.speaker: Text to CNO, 09:48 — ICU Charge Nurse
transcript.text: The ICU sepsis protocol still defaults to KVO at 40 mL/h and a 250 mL minibag for every antibiotic, and the residents are signing it as is. Pharmacy keeps bouncing them and the residents are asking which default is right.

voiceStyles.Infusion Center Manager: Woman in her 50s, experienced oncology nurse, calm but clipped and under time pressure, low chatter of a busy infusion room behind her
voiceStyles.Text to CNO, 09:48 — ICU Charge Nurse: Read flatly as a text message on the CNO's phone

instructorNote: This tests two things. First, the CMO should decide the Chair 4 patient using the clinical priority order: chemotherapy cannot safely wait. The decision should not rest on the cabinet restriction. Pharmacy then acts on the ruling and adds her to the patients-affected count. Second, the CNO and CMO should send one notice to the units and about 90 physicians by email, text and huddle script, with the same numbers in all three. Watch whether that notice withdraws Memos A and B, sets flushes per PH-22-A (saline locks with prefilled syringes, no KVO) and gives the current 4.9 days on hand, and whether the CMO and CNO get the KVO and minibag defaults removed from the ICU order set.
